Markets.title: Muthoot Finance Q2 cons profit jumps 36% YoY to Rs 3,278 crore
Markets.summary: Muthoot Finance reported a 36% year-on-year increase in consolidated net profit to Rs 3,278 crore for the second quarter, alongside a 42% growth in assets under management to Rs 2.09 lakh crore. However, the company experienced a deterioration in asset quality as its standalone gross NPA ratio rose to 3.87% from 2.28% in the previous quarter.

Markets.title: Sebi to release FII compliance consultation paper within weeks, says chairman Tuhin Kanta Pandey
Markets.summary: Markets regulator Sebi plans to release a consultation paper within weeks to align foreign investor compliance norms with global standards. This initiative comes amid heavy foreign institutional investor outflows and includes plans to strengthen independent directors' effectiveness.

Markets.title: US bonds rally, sending yields to biggest monthly decline since 2023
Markets.summary: US Treasuries rallied as a technology stock selloff driven by disappointing earnings from Amazon and Intel pushed investors toward safer assets. This shift sent the 10-year note yield to its largest monthly drop in nearly three years, even as expectations for a December interest rate hike remained high.

Markets.title: NTPC Q2 Results: Standalone profit rises 14% YoY to Rs 5,320 crore; revenue up 17%
Markets.summary: NTPC reported a 14% year-on-year increase in standalone net profit to Rs 5,320 crore for the second quarter of FY27, alongside a 16.8% rise in revenue. The company also announced an interim dividend of Rs 3 per share and plans to increase its capital expenditure.

Markets.title: Dalal Street Weak Ahead: Nifty stands on firmer footing, but can it break past 23,450?
Markets.summary: The Nifty gained two percent last week to recover above its crucial 200-week moving average. Analysts warn that bearish momentum indicates caution as the index faces immediate resistance between 23,300 and 23,450.

Markets.title: CDSL Q2 results: Net profit jumps 24% YoY to Rs 173 crore, revenue up 24%
Markets.summary: Central Depository Services Ltd (CDSL) reported a 24% year-on-year increase in Q2 net profit to Rs 173 crore alongside a 24% rise in revenue to Rs 395 crore. During the quarter, the depository added about 75 lakh new demat accounts, pushing its assets under custody past Rs 89 lakh crore.

Geo-Political.title: 'We came back from hell', say Ukrainians after years in Russia-occupied frontline city
Geo-Political.summary: An evacuated Ukrainian couple described their years living in the Russia-occupied frontline city of Oleshky as "hell." The pair stated they had to cross minefields in the city just to search for food.

Geo-Political.title: Ukrainian evacuees reunite with family after years trapped in Russia-occupied city
Geo-Political.summary: Ukrainian evacuees from the Russian-occupied city of Oleshky have reunited with their families after enduring years without food, water, or electricity. During their time trapped in the city, many residents were forced to cook garden weeds just to survive.

Geo-Political.title: Crypto firm Binance covers 90% of losses after $6.3bn hack
Geo-Political.summary: Cryptocurrency exchange Binance is covering 90% of user losses following a massive $6.3 billion hack. Two analytics firms state that intelligence points to a North Korean state-backed group as the likely perpetrator.

Geo-Political.title: More than 5,000 die from Ebola in DR Congo's deadliest outbreak
Geo-Political.summary: More than 5,000 people have died in the Democratic Republic of Congo during its deadliest Ebola outbreak. Government data shows that over 10,000 individuals have contracted the rare virus.

Geo-Political.title: Police deployed during stand-off over control of top Poland court
Geo-Political.summary: Police were deployed during a stand-off for control of Poland's top court. This escalation occurred after the government suspended two senior justices and moved to bring criminal charges against them.

Geo-Political.title: Ethiopian PM puts ministers through military training
Geo-Political.summary: Ethiopian Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed has required his government ministers to undergo military training. This initiative aligns with his prior emphasis on military preparedness as a key goal for his administration.

Data & Insights.title: Govt scraps export duty on petrol; hikes levies on diesel, ATF — check details here
Data & Insights.summary: India eliminated the export duty on petrol for a two-week period starting October 31. Simultaneously, the government increased export levies on diesel and aviation turbine fuel (ATF).

Data & Insights.title: India lifted 49.6 crore people out of poverty between 2011 and 2023, says World Bank report - Here is how it was done
Data & Insights.summary: Between 2011 and 2023, the World Bank reported that India lifted 496 million people out of poverty. This reduction dropped extreme poverty from 27.1% to 2.6% through consumption growth, increased employment, and expanded social programs.

Data & Insights.title: Govt sets up high-level banking panel under Suresh N. Patel
Data & Insights.summary: The Indian government has established a high-level banking panel led by Suresh N. Patel to review the country's banking sector. The committee will recommend reforms to make the sector globally competitive, financially inclusive, and resilient by 2047.

Data & Insights.title: Extreme poverty in India falls to 2.6% from 27.1%: World Bank
Data & Insights.summary: Between 2011 and 2023, 496 million people in India rose above the lower-middle-income poverty line. Consequently, the World Bank reported that extreme poverty in the country dropped from 27.1% to 2.6%.

Data & Insights.title: ‘2026 resembles 1991’: Why CEA V Anantha Nageswaran wants India to rethink its growth strategy — what he said
Data & Insights.summary: Chief Economic Adviser V Anantha Nageswaran warned that global tensions and supply shocks require India to rethink its growth strategy. He urged the country to build stronger domestic capabilities, diversify its imports, and create strategic resource buffers.

Data & Insights.title: West Asia conflict drives 15-20% surge in working capital demand at Indian banks, lifts corporate credit growth: Report
Data & Insights.summary: The West Asia conflict has increased working-capital demand at Indian banks by 15 to 20 percent due to rising raw-material costs and shipping delays. This surge, along with refinancing and acquisition-related borrowing, has driven corporate credit growth during the September quarter.

India.title: Case Against School After Boy, 8, Assaults 6-Year-Old Girl In Haryana
India.summary: Haryana police filed a case against a school after an eight-year-old boy allegedly assaulted a six-year-old girl. Preliminary investigations revealed negligence by the school management regarding security and student supervision.

India.title: BJP Leader's Singer Wife, A Kabir Bhajan, And Some 'Jantar Mantar': How 15th Century Saint Entered 2026 Row
India.summary: A viral singing performance by BJP leader's wife Sivasri Skandaprasad was misinterpreted as a political dig at protests at Delhi's Jantar Mantar. The song actually features 15th-century saint Kabir's spiritual lyrics, which used the phrase "jantar mantar" in a profound, non-political sense.

India.title: 36 Villas, 2 Cities, Rs 5 Crore: Rajasthan IAS-IPS Couple Under Probe
India.summary: A Rajasthan IAS-IPS couple is under investigation for alleged financial links with the directors of Goyal Fashions Private Limited, a hospitality company operating Ananta brand hotels and resorts. The probe is examining assets that reportedly include 36 villas across two cities valued at 5 crore rupees.

India.title: Cop's Mutilated Body Recovered From Railway Tracks In Bengal
India.summary: A police officer's mutilated body was recovered from railway tracks in West Bengal. Previously, on February 20, 2025, he had survived a self-inflicted gunshot wound in Howrah.

India.title: At Adani University Convocation, Priti Adani Calls For Ethical AI Use
India.summary: Priti Adani urged the ethical use of artificial intelligence during the Adani University convocation ceremony. IISc Director Professor Govindan Rangarajan attended the event as the chief guest alongside other academic leaders and families.

India.title: Ground Report: Thousands Relocated In Bengal After Lake Burst In Bhutan
India.summary: Thousands of residents in West Bengal's Sankosh Forest Village were relocated following a flash flood caused by a lake burst in Bhutan. The flood brought muddy water and dead fish, inundating the local river since Saturday morning.

General.title: Ukrainian evacuees reunite with family after years trapped in Russia-occupied city
General.summary: Ukrainian evacuees from the Russian-occupied city of Oleshky reunited with their families after surviving years without food, water, and electricity. Residents in the besieged city had resorted to cooking garden weeds to stay alive.

General.title: Emotional reunions with loved ones for Oleshky evacuees
General.summary: Evacuated residents from Oleshky arrived at the northern Ukrainian border with Belarus in buses and ambulances following a temporary ceasefire. BBC journalist Dan Johnson traveled to the location to witness their emotional reunions with loved ones.

General.title: Healey risks breaking minimum wage promise for younger workers
General.summary: Chancellor Healey suggested that younger workers might not receive the same minimum wage as older adults before the next election. This potential policy difference risks breaking a previous government promise regarding equal pay for younger employees.

General.title: 'It's been killing me!' Celebrity Traitors winners relieved the secret is out
General.summary: The second series finale of The Celebrity Traitors drew 11.2 million live viewers on Friday. The winners expressed immense relief that they can finally talk about their victory after keeping it a secret.

General.summary: British Prime Minister Sir Keir Starmer stated that Europe can no longer depend on the United States to fund its defense. He warned that transatlantic relations are permanently changed now that Washington expects allies to pay their own way.
